lesson: Stock is bought against caps on capital, not against an empty shelf.
evidence: 1.1M of the 5M start went into stock in ten minutes: every one of 140 categories had a 'no stock yet' bonus

lesson: The guardian never pays above the unit's list price whatever the budget, and an offer above the ask becomes the ask.
evidence: a 28,900 unit was bought at 30,500: the category reference sat above the SKU's list price

lesson: A number in a shop's message is an ask only inside 0.2-3x of the list price.
evidence: 179 of 535 stored asks were weights and counts such as '120g x 20'

lesson: Demand is flat around the clock here; what changes is supply per category, so posture follows category scarcity, not the hour.
evidence: about 150 orders an hour day and night; sofas: two thirds of visits found the unit gone, kimchi: none

lesson: One bad row does not blacklist a shop: two rows and a tenth of its deals do, and a receipt may name any acceptable SKU.
evidence: 43 honest deals were marked dishonest and 30 of the biggest shops were skipped for 1.5 days; fill 16% against a market median of 44%

lesson: A break without a warranty costs the whole deal; goods go to shops whose goods carry one.
evidence: 32 unrefunded breaks; every break under a warranty was refunded, 36 of 36

lesson: At the same shop the top buyers pay what I pay; the score comes from which shops are visited and how many orders close, so a close moves the order to the next shop.
evidence: Kiro729: they paid 0.57-0.61 of list, I paid 0.62; they closed 60-70% of orders, I closed 18%, 47% of mine ended at the first shop's refusal

lesson: Every skip list needs an expiry.
evidence: 48 shops were cooled off for good, among them nocha12 (10,756 settles a day) and psyoung82 (8,053); 14 of one order's 23 candidates

lesson: A model round is worth its tokens only where the shop moves; the model is not asked when the shop concedes under 3%.
evidence: 129 Haiku offers in 25 minutes drew 127 counters and 2 deals

lesson: The scoring rule is part of the environment: it is read from the market's rules page and never written into code or a prompt.
evidence: patch 3.6 (11-12 17:41) made the score the share of the shop's margin kept; for five days the agent bought for the old one: grade C at 0.565 of list scored 0.63, grade A at 0.665 scored 0.91

lesson: A fact that decisions depend on is written down in a profile a person can open, not recomputed from the whole order log on every order.
evidence: 103,368 rows, 57 MB: 2.5 s of a 5.5 s median order went to re-reading them; the blacklist and cooling-off bugs were such recomputed facts

lesson: Shops differ in whether they bargain at all; each shop's acceptance threshold is remembered and a fixed-price shop is paid its ask or left without an offer.
evidence: 22,883 visits: YAHO1212, nocha12, bjeon01, 25620027 accept at 1.00 of the ask and nothing lower; psyoung82 at 0.83, ddolcom at 0.70

lesson: The shop's own log records agreements, not settlements; a comparison built on it is noise until it is checked against the ledger.
evidence: 11-16 the log shows 167.9M revenue at a 69% margin while the board's Book rose about 1.4M a day; the tuner moved seller_volume_share 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.6, 0.7 on that comparison

lesson: Stock that does not sell is capital that does not turn; holding it at cost keeps the Book and ends the business.
evidence: 33.4M of stock at a median age of 170 h, 68% older than 120 h; deals fell from 1,190 a day (11-10) to about 400; Book grew 8.4M in six days

lesson: An unattended model needs a login that does not expire, and a failed call must raise an alarm a person sees.
evidence: the subscription login reached its time limit on 11-15 21:48: 1,150 bargaining calls and the reflections of 11-16 and 11-17 got no answer until a person logged in again on 11-17 19:10; the code fallback kept trading and nothing said so
